provenance.instrument: Lower Salford Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 164 Zoning, Ord. No. 8 of 1956, amended in its entirety by Ord. No. 62-6 of 1962, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 LO0727: 'Includes legislation through 05-06-2026'. New Laws not yet in the code: Ord. No. 2026-06 and Ord. No. 2026-07 (both 8-5-2026, zoning amendments).
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 05-06-2026'. The chapter page lists New Laws Ord. No. 2026-06 and 2026-07 (Zoning Amendment, adopted 2026-08-05).
provenance.code_caution: Two zoning ordinances adopted 8-5-2026 are not yet in the online code and were read only in the site's search excerpts (their PDFs were not opened). Ord. No. 2026-06 adds an Age-Qualified Residential (AQR) development for people 55 and older in the LPOD overlay by conditional use, on 35 acres, with single-family detached, two-family and triplex dwellings, and amends 164-28.1 to 164-28.4 and the zoning map. Ord. No. 2026-07 creates a Data Center Overlay District over I District land along Wambold Road. Neither excerpt touches a second unit on a house lot. The R-4 dimensional table (Attachment 3) and the neighborhood development option table (Attachment 4) are PDFs and were not opened, so R-4 lot figures are not on file.
checks: The zoning code has no accessory dwelling unit, in-law suite or similar term. No district lists a second dwelling unit on a single-family lot and the code has no special exception for unlisted uses: R-1A, R-1, R-3, C and MU list their uses 'and no other', and the other districts list theirs as the uses a lot may have. So a second unit needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (164-133C) unless one of the two-family paths below fits. The Board may also interpret whether a questionable use is permitted (164-133A)

A dwelling unit is for one family with 'one exclusive cooking facility', and every dwelling unit must be in a single-family detached building (one unit), a two-family building, a single-family attached building or an apartment building. A lot holds one principal building (164-5), though VC sets standards for two or more principal buildings on one lot (164-70.3B). So a house with a second unit is a two-family building

In R-1, 'Alteration of a single-family dwelling into a two-family dwelling' is a conditional use before the Board of Supervisors (164-30B(3), 164-25). The code sets no further standards for it. R-2 permits 'any of the uses or purposes permitted in an R-1 Residence District' (164-38A) and C permits 'A use permitted in R-2 Residence Districts' (164-64A). Whether that carries the R-1 conditional use into R-2 and C is not settled: ask the township

In VC a two-family dwelling (twin or duplex) is permitted by right. VC allows six dwelling units per acre, and 164-5 measures density per gross acre, so two units need about 14,520 sq ft of gross lot. Conversions need public sewer (164-5, 164-70.2A(2), 164-70.3, 164-70.4G)

In R-4 and R-5 a two-family building is permitted on a lot within a tract proposed for development, with 15% common open space and public sewer and water (R-5: a 5-acre tract, 4,500 sq ft per unit). In OLC two-family and triplex buildings are permitted only as a development on 10 acres. In RO an existing home may be converted into a professional office and one apartment as a conditional use (164-46, 164-54, 164-55, 164-62.9H, 164-62.16A(2))

An accessory building on a house lot must stand at least 10 ft behind the house and 10 ft from all other buildings on the lot, be no larger than 30% of the house's floor area (more by conditional use on a 60,000 sq ft lot) and meet setbacks that grow with its size: 5 ft (100 sq ft and 9 ft tall), 10 ft (500 sq ft and 15 ft), the house setbacks above that. In R-3, and so on an OLC house lot, accessory buildings are at most 15 ft and one story (164-15B(1), 164-42H(2), 164-43C(7)(b), 164-44C(7)(b), 164-62.9A)
An owner who lives in the house may rent rooms to no more than two nontransient persons (164-15B(7)). That is not a separate dwelling unit

In OLC a house follows the R-3 standards (164-62.9A), while the OLC table's by-right column gives other figures (front 30, side 20, rear 40, 60 ft from abutting residential lot lines, building coverage 10%, green space 60%, 164-62.12). The stricter of each is shown: ask which set applies
In C a house lot takes only the R-2 area and width (32,500 sq ft, 125 ft, 164-66). The code states no yards, building coverage or height for an exclusive residential use there: ask

status.note: No ADU text. No district lists a second unit on a house lot, and the code has no special exception for unlisted uses (R-1A, R-1, R-3, C and MU list their uses 'and no other', the others list the uses a lot may have). A dwelling unit must sit in a single-family detached, two-family, single-family attached or apartment building, and a single-family detached building holds a single dwelling unit, so a house with a second unit becomes a two-family building. That is a conditional use in R-1 (alteration of a single-family dwelling into a two-family dwelling) and by right in VC (see the alternatives).

path.note: A second unit on a single-family lot is not a listed use in any district, so it needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board on a showing of unnecessary hardship (164-133C, MPC 910.2). No section bars use variances. Where the code lists a two-family dwelling, making the house into one is the listed path instead (R-1 conditional use, VC by right).

fallback_path.note: The Zoning Hearing Board may authorize a variance 'where, owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the provisions of this chapter will result in unnecessary hardship'. No special exception for unlisted uses was found. The Board may interpret whether a questionable use is permitted as similar or customarily incidental to a permitted use (164-133A), and C permits by conditional use 'Any use of the same general character as any of the above permitted uses' (164-64J(1)).

disputed_districts.note: R-2 permits 'any of the uses or purposes permitted in an R-1 Residence District' and C 'A use permitted in R-2 Residence Districts'. Whether that includes the R-1 conditional use (164-30B) is not settled

value.conditions: Conditional use before the Board of Supervisors after a public hearing, which may attach reasonable conditions (164-25). The code sets no specific standards for the alteration. The lot keeps the district figures: in R-1 a net lot of 45,000 sq ft, 150 ft wide, yards 75/30/50 ft, building area 9%, 35 ft (R-2 and C residential lots 32,500 sq ft). Two parking spaces per dwelling unit.

requires.condition: An existing single-family dwelling is altered

value.note: Not an ADU listing. No family or owner rule. The result is a two-family building (two dwelling units in one building, 164-5)

value.name: Two-family dwelling (VC)
value.conditions: A two-family dwelling (twin or duplex) is permitted by right in VC. Net lot at least 10,000 sq ft and 60 ft wide, and residential density at most six dwelling units per acre (7.5 with bonuses), measured per gross acre (164-5), so two units need about 14,520 sq ft of gross lot. Impervious cover (buildings and paving) at most 80% of the net lot, 40 ft or 3.5 stories, side yards 10 ft, rear 20 ft, front 15 to 25 ft from the ultimate right-of-way. 'All new developments and conversions shall be served by public sewer facilities.' Two parking spaces per dwelling unit.
value.note: Not an ADU listing. The 14,520 sq ft figure is the six units per gross acre density applied to two units, a reading. The VC intent names the conversion of existing buildings. 164-70.3B also sets standards for two or more principal buildings on one lot

value.name: Two-family building in an R-4 tract development
value.conditions: On a lot within a tract proposed for development: one single-family detached dwelling or one two-family building, among other types. Base density three units per gross acre (four with bonuses, five in a fully mixed development), 15% of the tract as common open space when two-family units are built, public sewer and water, 2.5 off-street parking spaces per unit (garages not counted). Lot figures for fee-simple lots are in Attachment 3, which was not read.
value.note: Not an ADU listing. A development use. Whether an existing house lot alone can be made into a two-family building under it is not settled

value.name: Two-family building in an R-5 tract development
value.conditions: Two-family buildings need a tract of at least 5 gross acres, three units per gross acre (four with bonuses), lots of 4,500 sq ft per unit, 35 ft wide per lot and 20 ft per unit, 30% building coverage, rear yard 25 ft, side 15 ft, 15% common open space, public sewer and water, two parking spaces per unit (2.2 when lotted).
value.note: Not an ADU listing. A development use on 5 acres, not a unit added to one house

value.name: Two-family and triplex development (OLC)
value.conditions: A mixed residential development of unlotted two-family and triplex buildings on a tract of at least 10 gross acres with frontage on two roads, at most 5.5 units per acre, 15% common open space, public sewer and water, 2.5 parking spaces per unit.
value.note: Not an ADU listing. A development use on 10 acres

value.name: Existing home converted into a professional office and one apartment (RO)
value.conditions: Class One conditional use: 'Conversion of an existing home into a professional office and one apartment'. Lot at least 30,000 sq ft and 125 ft wide, public sewer and public water, the existing building built for residential use preserved, expansion at most 50% of its floor area, residential character, no parking in front yards.
value.note: Not an ADU listing. The house becomes an office with one apartment, so it is not a second unit beside a house

value.name: Offices and one apartment (RO Class Two)
value.conditions: Class Two conditional use 'Offices and one apartment'. Lot at least 80,000 sq ft and 150 ft wide, front 40 ft, side 30 ft, rear 40 ft, with the other RO Class Two standards.
value.note: Not an ADU listing. An office use with one apartment, not a second unit beside a house
